intro: Educated German often means more than it says, and the listener or reader has to supply what is left unsaid. Each item in this quiz gives an utterance in its situation and asks what it does or means: a statement that is really a request („Ganz schön frisch hier drin“) or a hint to leave („Morgen ist ja leider wieder ein Arbeitstag“); litotes, which affirms by denying the opposite (a strict boss’s „Nicht schlecht“, „nicht unerheblich“, „nicht ganz ungefährlich“); veiled criticism („Da ist noch Luft nach oben“) and the coded language of German job references („Er bemühte sich …“); irony („Na, herrliches Wetter heute!“); fixed polite formulas whose real meaning is a rejection, an objection or nothing at all („Wir melden uns“, „Bei allem Respekt“, „Wir müssen mal essen gehen“); allusion to shared knowledge; the loaded question that presupposes guilt; the rhetorical question; and the judgement conveyed by what a writer leaves out. Your answer names the speech act or the meaning; synonyms that fit the sentence are accepted.
tips[0].title: Statements that do something else
tips[0].text: A statement about the situation is often a request or a signal: Ganz schön frisch hier (close the window) · Morgen ist ja wieder ein Arbeitstag (time to go – the guests verstehen den Wink) · Ich will Sie nicht länger aufhalten (goodbye) · Ich erinnere an … (an allusion: the speaker spielt auf etwas an). The test is always the situation: if the literal meaning is pointless there, look for the act.
tips[0].check.why: Her early start is pointless information for the guests, so the statement has another job: it is a polite signal to leave.
tips[1].title: Litotes and understatement
tips[1].text: Litotes negates the opposite: nicht unerheblich (= considerable), nicht unbegabt (= talented), nicht ohne (= demanding, impressive), nicht ganz ungefährlich (= dangerous), alles andere als leicht (= very hard). Understatement shrinks something big: Da ist noch Luft nach oben (= it is weak), Das war ein kleiner Rückschlag (= a disaster). How strong a litotes is depends on the speaker and the tone: from a sparing critic it can be high praise, from a polite one mere tact.
tips[1].trap: Do not read a litotes as mild: nicht unerheblich in an official report usually means large, and nicht ganz ungefährlich after a rescue means life-threatening.
tips[1].check.why: Litotes denies the opposite to affirm strongly: nicht ganz ungefährlich after a rescue means life-threatening.
tips[2].title: Irony, formulas and coded praise
tips[2].text: Irony says the opposite (Herrliches Wetter! in the rain; Sie sind ja früh dran to a latecomer). Polite formulas have fixed pragmatic meanings: Wir melden uns (often a rejection) · Bei allem Respekt (an objection follows) · Wir müssen mal essen gehen (a Floskel, not an invitation) · Ein … interessanter Ansatz with a pause (usually scepticism). German job references (Arbeitszeugnisse) must sound positive, so criticism is coded: Er bemühte sich (he failed), zu unserer Zufriedenheit (only adequate), zu unserer vollsten Zufriedenheit (very good).
tips[2].trap: Interessant and bei Gelegenheit are not always negative – intonation and situation decide. Treat them as signals to check, not as fixed translations.
tips[2].check.why: In the coded language of references, plain zu unserer Zufriedenheit is a weak grade; very good needs stets and vollsten.
tips[2].visual.rows[1].a: Sie trug zur Verbesserung des Betriebsklimas bei.
tips[2].visual.rows[1].b: She was sociable, perhaps too much.
tips[2].visual.rows[2].a: Er erledigte alle Aufgaben stets zu unserer vollsten Zufriedenheit.
tips[3].title: Presupposition, rhetorical questions, meaningful silence
tips[3].text: A loaded question presupposes what it should ask: Seit wann wissen Sie davon? unterstellt, dass jemand davon wusste. A rhetorical question expects no answer and makes a claim: Wer hätte das ahnen können? = niemand. And what is not said speaks too: a reference that praises only handwriting and punctuality fällt ein vernichtendes Urteil über die fachliche Eignung.
tips[3].check.why: A loaded question presupposes what it should ask: Seit wann only makes sense if the hiding already happened.
tips[4].title: Ask what the sentence does, not what it says
tips[4].text: Every utterance has a job: request, praise, rejection, objection, warning, reproach. If the literal meaning does not fit the situation, find the job – that is what the listening item asks for.
tips[4].check.why: The literal welcome does not fit forty minutes late, so look for the act: it is ironic criticism of the lateness.
remember[0]: Statement → request; litotes → strong affirmation; understatement → big problem.
remember[1]: Wir melden uns → often a rejection; Bei allem Respekt → objection; Er bemühte sich → he failed.
remember[2]: Loaded question presupposes; rhetorical question asserts; silence judges.
remember[3]: Find the job of the sentence, not its words.
mistakes[0].why: The formula postpones the answer; after a short interview it usually signals no.
mistakes[1].why: In reference-letter code, effort without result is a clear negative.
mistakes[2].why: Litotes affirms by denying the opposite: not insignificant = significant.
hook: Hear what Germans mean but never say: hints, litotes, irony and the coded praise of a job reference.
tips[0].check.q: Shortly after midnight the hostess yawns and says to her guests: „Morgen muss ich ja leider früh raus.“ What is she really doing?
tips[0].check.options[0]: Hinting that it is time to go
tips[0].check.options[1]: Inviting them to stay the night
tips[0].check.options[2]: Asking them to wake her up
tips[0].check.answer: Hinting that it is time to go
tips[1].check.q: After a rescue the mountain guide says: „Der Abstieg war nicht ganz ungefährlich.“ What does he mean?
tips[3].check.q: A journalist asks a manager: „Seit wann verschweigen Sie die Mängel?“ What does the question take for granted?
tips[3].check.options[0]: That he has been hiding the defects
tips[3].check.options[2]: That the journalist hid the defects
tips[3].check.answer: That he has been hiding the defects
tips[4].check.q: An employee walks into the 9 o'clock meeting at 9:40. The boss says: „Schön, dass Sie uns auch noch beehren.“ What is the job of this sentence?
